results.title: Mixed-bed polishing resin exhaustion
results.text: Exhausted ion-exchange resin lets ions break through, so resistivity drops quickly. Corrective action: replace or regenerate the resin bed, flush to rinse down, and verify resistivity recovers toward the limit before returning the loop to service.

results.title: AMC rising in a process bay
results.text: Compare AMC at the make-up air inlet with AMC in the bay. If the inlet is steady while the bay rises, the chemical filtration stage is the likely source.

results.title: Resistivity drop at point of use
results.text: A sudden fall in resistivity downstream of the polishing stage, with normal resistivity at the EDI outlet, points to the mixed-bed polishing resin. Compare resin runtime with its rated life. A gradual fall that follows rising RO permeate conductivity points upstream to the RO stage instead.

report.narrative: The ultra-pure water resistivity at point of use tag UPW_A_RES_POU measured 16.9343 MOhm.cm, which is below the limit of 18.2 MOhm.cm, resulting in a reading verdict of FAIL. The sensor calibration is valid. Runtime inspection for POLISH_A shows the mixed-bed resin has reached 5380 hours, which is 119.6 percent of its rated life of 4500 hours, exceeding its operational rating. In contrast, UV lamp runtime for UV_A is at 65.0 percent of rated life and RO membrane runtime for RO_A is at 58.3 percent of rated life. Knowledge base citations UPW-04 and UPW-03 indicate that mixed-bed polishing resin exhaustion causes a sudden fall in resistivity downstream of the polishing stage. Therefore, resin exhaustion is identified as the root cause.
recommended_actions: Review mixed-bed resin replacement procedures for POLISH_A.
Replace or regenerate the exhausted resin bed.
Flush the system to rinse down and verify resistivity recovers toward the limit before returning the loop to service.
